quotes.quote: my P(doom) is sort of infamously high, like 70%.
quotes.originalOutcome: AI doom, including loss of control and concentration of power
quotes.context: His definition includes dictatorship or oligarchy. No fixed horizon is attached to the 70% estimate. See the Race with China section, from 1:32:30.
Alexander explicitly says he does not count oligarchy as doom. No fixed horizon is attached to this estimate. It is not the probability of the specific AI 2027 scenario.

quotes.quote: 10% to 20% seemed like reasonable numbers to me.
quotes.originalOutcome: AI leading to human extinction within 30 years
quotes.context: Responding to a question framed around the next 30 years. He emphasizes uncertainty and that the numbers might change. Historical statement, not asserted to be his latest view.

quotes.sourceTitle: Paul Christiano: My views on doom
quotes.originalOutcome: Humanity irreversibly ruins its future within 10 years after powerful AI
quotes.context: Powerful AI means AI that makes human labor obsolete. Includes AI takeover, additional extinction risk and other permanent bad outcomes; 46% is not extinction alone.

quotes.sourceTitle: Paul Christiano: My views on doom
quotes.context: World governed by AI systems without adequately aligned values. Not necessarily human extinction. Includes takeover by later AI systems; no fixed calendar horizon.

quotes.quote: Probability that most humans die within 10 years
quotes.sourceTitle: Paul Christiano: My views on doom
quotes.originalOutcome: Most humans die within 10 years after powerful AI
quotes.context: Powerful AI means AI that makes human labor obsolete. Includes takeover and non-takeover causes during rapid change. Most humans dying is not identical to extinction.

quotes.quote: I got around, like, 20 per cent probability that it turns out catastrophic.
quotes.context: Historical 2023 estimate. His reasoning included human-level AI within a decade and AI or humans using it against humanity. In a May 2026 80,000 Hours interview he declined to give an updated p(doom), so this must not be presented as his current estimate.

quotes.quote: I’d rather stay out of the p(doom) game.
quotes.originalOutcome: Whether to update his earlier AI catastrophe estimate
quotes.context: Asked whether his 2023 estimate of 20% had changed, he declined to give a new probability. Recorded April 16, 2026; published May 7. His concerns remain substantial, but this is not a new numerical forecast.

quotes.quote: No, no, not zero. Maybe, like, 15 percent.
quotes.sourceTitle: Hard Fork interview, reproduced by co-host Casey Newton
quotes.originalOutcome: Probability that AI kills us all
quotes.context: Answer to Kevin Roose asking the probability that AI will kill us all. No time horizon stated. Platformer reproduces the interview exchange and links the original episode.

quotes.quote: the probability of such a dystopian future is something like 10% or 20%.
quotes.sourceTitle: Peter Diamandis: Elon on Abundance, AI & Human Survival
quotes.context: Approximate range as stated in an Abundance Summit conversation. No fixed risk horizon. Musk says the positive scenario is more probable than the negative.

quotes.quote: There's a 25% chance that things go really, really badly
35 to 40% for any AI-mediated existential catastrophe.
quotes.sourceTitle: Eli Lifland interview with Ozzie Gooen
quotes.context: Historical estimate in a discussion of risk by 2070. He distinguishes his earlier 30% estimate for intent misalignment from 35–40% for any AI-mediated existential catastrophe, and suggests possible revisions. Do not label it 35% exactly.

quotes.quote: well in line with the expert consensus
quotes.sourceTitle: Nate Silver: It’s time to come to grips with AI
quotes.originalOutcome: Civilization destroys itself or enters a dystopia because of misaligned AI
quotes.context: He describes his own estimate as in line with a 5–10% expert range, rather than directly stating exact personal bounds. Kept qualitative rather than assigning an invented numeric point.

quotes.quote: I think there’s a 0% chance of AGI doom. Zero.
quotes.context: At 2:29:30. In context he distinguishes autonomous AGI doom from humans misusing technology. No fixed time horizon stated.

quotes.quote: I would say my p(doom) is about 10%.
quotes.originalOutcome: AGI or ASI destroys all human civilization
quotes.context: At 44:34, Fridman supplies his own probability before asking Sundar Pichai. This is Fridman’s estimate, not Pichai’s. No fixed horizon stated.

quotes.quote: The debate on existential risk is very premature
quotes.sourceTitle: Financial Times; excerpt collected by Finding Consensus
quotes.originalOutcome: Whether current AI development warrants existential-risk concerns
quotes.context: Qualitative statement. Finding Consensus’s 0 value was an editorial position on a different policy question, not a personal 0% extinction forecast. Original article is paywalled; excerpt verified against the existing public Finding Consensus record.

quotes.quote: this will discourage the release of open models, and make AI less competitive and less safe.
quotes.sourceTitle: TIME; excerpt collected by Finding Consensus
quotes.context: Policy quote about open-model regulation. It does not state a probability of AI doom. Original page could not be fetched; excerpt verified against the public Finding Consensus record.

researchNote: Historical public statements from 2023–2026, checked 2026-09-15. Public figures did not answer the AI Impacts survey question; all comparisons are related, with original outcomes and horizons retained. Finding Consensus’s 63 public records across six questions concern SB1047; its editorial values must never be treated as p(doom). Shared-source direct quote totals are limited to 25 words.
